name: Memory and Storage
blurb: HBM, DRAM, SSDs, and the storage tiers behind training runs.

items.name: WEKA
items.note: Parallel filesystem for AI training I/O; feeds GPU clusters at hyperscale customers

reading.body:
Memory and storage are now the critical path for AI training, not compute itself. The bottleneck has shifted from GPU count to feeding data fast enough that those GPUs stay busy.

High Bandwidth Memory sits directly on the GPU die and moves data to compute cores at speeds that match their throughput. SK hynix supplies the primary HBM for NVIDIA's datacenter processors, with Micron as the sole US alternative for H200 and Blackwell. This duopoly means HBM supply constrains how many training chips can actually run at rated speed. A shortage here stalls entire clusters.

Storage tiers behind the GPU tell a parallel story. VAST Data and WEKA handle the layer between bulk storage and GPU memory, moving terabytes per second through parallel filesystems designed for AI workloads. These are not generic storage; they are built specifically to prevent the disk from starving the accelerator. CoreWeave's GPU clusters run on VAST, indicating that even bare-metal cloud operators depend on specialized platforms to make their hardware coherent.

This data does not reveal how often memory or storage actually become the bottleneck in practice, or how capacity utilization compares across different training runs. It shows the components exist and where they sit in the stack. The constraint is real only if these pieces are oversubscribed or undersized relative to GPU appetite.
